brief.description: One practical late nineteenth-century PROSPECTING ROD: straight slender iron probe with a pointed steel tip at lower left, one continuous visible cool gray metal shaft, and a short warm brown wooden T-grip at upper right perpendicular to shaft. The grip is a single solid wooden crossbar, attached at its center by a small iron socket; no brass. Sturdy simple hand tool, length about four times grip width. Broad wood grain marks, clear shaft edges. Entire tool on a diagonal from lower left to upper right. No wires, dial, glow, gears, brush bristles or shovel blade.
